President Bola Tinubu on Sunday donated N250 million to families of victims of Friday’s boat accident in Bayelsa State. He ordered stricter enforcement of safety standards on inland waterways, as the death toll from the accident rose to 29, with more than 50 survivors. The accident occurred on Friday at the Oweikorogha/Otuan River Junction in Southern Ijaw Local Government Area, when a boat carrying scores of mourners travelling to a funeral capsized. Vice President Kashim Shettima conveyed the President’s position and the donation on Sunday during a condolence visit to Government House, Yenagoa, the state capital. This is according to a statement signed Sunday by Senior Special Assistant to the Vice President on Media and Communications, Stanley Nkwocha, titled ‘Bayelsa Boat Mishap: President Tinubu Orders Stiffer Waterway Safety Measures.’ Governor Douye Diri, who briefed the Vice President at Government House, attributed the tragedy to an alleged failure by boat operators to observe established safety protocols, describing it as avoidable. He said the state government had constituted a committee to investigate the immediate and remote causes of the accident. Shettima said Tinubu had also demanded a thorough investigation into the circumstances of the mishap, including preliminary reports of a possible mechanical fault. He stated, “We have received preliminary reports concerning the circumstances of this accident, including indications of a possible mechanical failure. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Geography may determine how people travel, but it must never determine how much protection their lives deserve. “A Nigerian travelling by boat is entitled to the same concern for safety as one travelling by road or air,” he said. The VP described the tragedy as carrying “a particular cruelty,” noting that the victims had set out to mourn the dead before death claimed them along the way. Somewhere, a family is struggling to understand how someone who left home for a funeral will never walk through that door again.” He assured the bereaved families that they would receive lasting support from the Federal Government. “To the families who have lost their loved ones, I will not pretend that time alone will make this pain disappear. “Our responsibility is to stand with you beyond this visit, beyond these condolences and beyond the days when this tragedy dominates the news,” he said. Before proceeding to Government House, the VP visited survivors receiving treatment at the Bayelsa Medical University Teaching Hospital, where he consoled patients and assured them of adequate medical care. Shettima commended the governor for visiting the accident scene and coordinating the state’s response. He acknowledged the efforts of the National Emergency Management Agency, the Bayelsa State Emergency Management Agency, the Nigerian Red Cross Society, the Nigeria Police Force, the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps, local divers and community volunteers. Diri announced that the state government had taken responsibility for the medical bills of all survivors and assured bereaved families they would not be abandoned. On arrival in Yenagoa, Shettima was received by the governor, the Minister of State for Petroleum Resources, Senator Heineken Lokpobiri; the Managing Director of the Niger Delta Development Commission, Dr Samuel Ogbuku; Bayelsa State APC Chairman, Dr Dennis Otiotio; and the Managing Director, Niger Delta River Basin Development Authority, Ebitimi Amgbare, among others. On Saturday, Tinubu called for a minute of silence in honour of victims of the boat accident during the All Progressives Congress campaign rally in Oyo State. The President made the announcement while addressing supporters at the rally, where he called for prayers for the repose of the victims’ souls and an end to similar incidents. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, also called for an immediate investigation into the remote and direct causes of the fatal boat mishap Oyetola, in a statement released on Sunday through his media aide, Dr Bolaji Akinola, directed the National Inland Waterways Authority to “conduct a thorough investigation into the incident and submit its report to him.” Also, former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has called on the Federal and Bayelsa State governments to investigate the boat mishap that claimed several lives in the Southern Ijaw Local Government Area of Bayelsa State recently. He also called for improved safety regulations across the nation’s waterways.
